quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 PRELIMINARY results (DART preliminary-results disclosure filed 08-06-2026, consolidated, K-IFRS, continuing operations; period 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30): revenue KRW 346,873M, +5.7% QoQ (Q1 2026: KRW 328,086M) and +17.5% YoY (Q2 2025: KRW 295,226M); operating profit KRW 59,290M, -11.0% QoQ (Q1: KRW 66,593M) but +38.9% YoY (Q2 2025: KRW 42,687M) - a 17.1% OP margin; pre-tax profit KRW 89,946M (+2,928.5% YoY vs KRW 2,970M); net profit KRW 84,971M (+27.0% QoQ, +1,450.6% YoY); net profit attributable to owners KRW 86,141M (+26.2% QoQ, +1,153.9% YoY). MIX (H1 external revenue): electronic materials KRW 625,340M = 92.6% of sales - of which SEMICONDUCTOR materials KRW 450,426M (66.7%), DISPLAY materials KRW 164,473M (24.4%), secondary-battery materials KRW 10,226M (1.5%), other KRW 215M; foaming agents (blowing agents, now housed in the Dongjin Innochem subsidiary spun off 01-01-2026) KRW 48,844M (7.2%); refined-oil recycling KRW 745M. By reporting segment: domestic electronic materials revenue KRW 617,438M with segment OP KRW 134,117M (21.7% margin, up from KRW 105,928M in H1 2025); overseas electronic materials KRW 93,906M with an OP LOSS of KRW 10,769M (narrowed from a KRW 17,603M loss - the US Texas start-ups DSM Semichem LLC and Dongjin Semichem Texas plus Dongjin Sweden AB); foaming agents OP loss KRW 1,728M; overseas holding companies OP KRW 4,615M. GEOGRAPHY by customer location: Korea KRW 569,332M (84.4%), China KRW 80,970M (12.0%), US KRW 15,682M (2.3%), Taiwan KRW 8,938M (1.3%), Japan KRW 38M; exports (incl. local L/C exports to Samsung and LG Display) KRW 527,585M = 78.17% of sales, domestic KRW 147,375M = 21.83%. DISCONTINUED China electronic-materials operations (10 subsidiaries held for sale): H1 revenue KRW 184,884M, OP KRW 27,746M, profit KRW 22,315M; assets held for sale KRW 340,056M. Balance sheet 2026-06-30: cash KRW 411,569M plus short-term financial assets KRW 92,446M; borrowings KRW 651,202M (short-term KRW 482,875M); net debt KRW 256,275M, gearing ratio 17.10% (down from 21.18%); equity KRW 1,242,362M; H1 operating cash flow KRW 151,197M (vs KRW 110,491M); inventories rose to KRW 232,185M from KRW 194,272M (raw materials KRW 103,510M). Employees 1,369 (06-30-2026). Q1 2026 reference: revenue KRW 328,086M, OP KRW 66,593M; FY2025: revenue KRW 1,194,145M, OP KRW 172,449M.

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and customers (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026, as of 06-30-2026): the company holds NO separate order or supply contracts and no order backlog - photoresist and other electronic materials are supplied to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and other chip/flat-panel makers under BASIC (master) supply agreements at an average of about KRW 104.4B PER MONTH (~KRW 1.25T annualised), and foaming agents to domestic/overseas customers at about KRW 8.1B per month; seasonal order swings are described as minimal. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (H1 2026 consolidated, continuing ops): SAMSUNG ELECTRONICS KRW 419,197M = 62.11% of revenue, SK HYNIX KRW 80,442M = 11.92%, LG DISPLAY KRW 35,514M = 5.26% - top three = 79.3%; the notes state customers each above 10% of group revenue totalled KRW 499,638M in H1 2026 vs KRW 413,554M in H1 2025 (+20.8%). Filing text: the semiconductor-materials customer base is 'two companies, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix'; display materials go to LG Display and Samsung Display plus Chinese panel makers (BOE, CSOT) whose Gen-10 fabs are ramping; the domestic market is 3-5 customers so overseas expansion is required. Sales channel: 73.99% of product sales are local exports (Samsung/LG Display order -> Dongjin delivery -> purchase confirmation/L/C -> payment), 3.77% domestic direct; direct sales are ~70% of product sales with domestic terms 75% cash / 25% 3-month notes, local exports 100% via purchase confirmations and master L/Cs; ~60% of sales are export-oriented, with agents in the US, Germany, Japan and Taiwan. Trade receivables KRW 140,542M gross (0.73% allowance), 90.9% under 6 months old. Separate-entity major-customer sales (>10%) KRW 480,034M of KRW 617,437M in H1 2026 vs KRW 284,542M a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: No contract backlog; ~KRW 104.4B/month electronic-materials supply under master agreements; H1 2026 Samsung 62.11% (KRW 419,197M), SK Hynix 11.92% (KRW 80,442M), LG Display 5.26%; >10% customers KRW 499,638M (+20.8% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity, utilisation and capex (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026, as of 06-30-2026): UTILISATION Q2 2026 - semiconductor electronic materials (Balan plant) 95.1%, display electronic materials (Balan and Incheon plants) 42.9% (capacity = 24-hour max daily output x 30 days). Domestic sites: Incheon (HQ), Balan/Hwaseong (semiconductor and display materials), Siheung (foaming agents, now Dongjin Innochem), Eumseong, Yesan (Sinam refinery); overseas: 11 China plants (Beijing, Chengdu, Hefei, Qidong, Xi'an - semiconductor thinner, Ordos, Chongqing, Huizhou, Fuzhou, Sichuan, Wuhan), Taiwan (Changhua), Sweden (Skelleftea - battery materials), US (DSM Semichem LLC in Plainview TX and Dongjin Semichem Texas in Killeen TX - electronic materials incl. sulphuric acid/thinner, funded by USD 74.2M of capital into Dongjin USA). PP&E KRW 827,027M with CONSTRUCTION IN PROGRESS KRW 364,037M (KRW 341,855M at year-end; KRW 32,229M added in H1); H1 PP&E additions KRW 42,387M (cash capex KRW 36,772M vs KRW 30,544M in H1 2025), machinery KRW 154,221M (+KRW 25,509M transferred from CIP). DSM Semichem's construction-in-progress (land, building, equipment KRW 131,753M) is pledged to Woori Bank against a KRW 32,372M facility loan; Dongjin USA carries a USD-denominated JPMorgan facility loan of KRW 49,328M maturing 05-08-2030. Company states no confirmed major new plant/equipment plans beyond investment tied to overseas subsidiaries' sales growth. RAW MATERIALS: solvents, PAC (photoactive compounds) and resins for photoresist/stripper/etchant production bought from Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Trading, PURAC Asia Pacific, Ashland and domestic suppliers Samyang NC Chem, Dongjin Advanced Materials (formerly Inos, a related party of the largest shareholder - H1 purchases KRW 34,231M) and Jaewon Industrial; H1 raw-material purchases KRW 387,678M, KRW 359,640M consumed in production; prices for solvents held roughly flat thanks to bulk-import discounts despite FX/oil moves. Filing text: material consumption rises with device stacking and larger wafer/glass areas; demand tracks the capex plans, fab expansions and utilisation of Samsung, SK Hynix and the panel makers.

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio, R&D and corporate events (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): (1) CHINA EXIT - on 06-16-2026 Dongjin Semichem and Dongjin Global Holdings contributed 100% of eight Chinese electronic-materials subsidiaries (Beijing incl. Ordos, Sichuan, Wuhan, Chengdu, Hefei, Chongqing, Fuzhou, Qidong) plus IP into a new Shanghai SPV, Dongjin Semichem (Shanghai) New Materials (capital CNY 1,405,116,011.63; parent 40.12%, Global Holdings 59.88%), and sold 70% of the SPV to Hefei Xin Dongjin New Material Technology (buyer changed by the 02-11-2026 board resolution from the Qingdao investor group approved 08-30-2025); joint sale price USD 134.1M with the parent's share ~USD 49.67M (1/2.7); the filing states this transaction has been COMPLETED, with a KRW 57,114M gain on disposal of subsidiary shares booked in the separate accounts in Q2; a separate 70% sale of Huizhou Dongjin is pending (both classified as discontinued). Dongjin retains 100% of the Xi'an thinner plant and Taiwan. (2) FOAMING-AGENT SPIN-OFF - blowing-agent business transferred to 100%-owned Dongjin Innochem on 01-01-2026 (KRW 187,877M net assets), leaving the parent a single electronic-materials segment. (3) JAPAN - Dongjin Japan Co. established 05-22-2026 (JPY 180M) and acquired 100% of TOKYO ELECTRONIC MATERIALS Co. on 05-27-2026 (a former related party that had been supplying Dongjin KRW 2,090M of materials in H1). (4) SHAREHOLDER RETURNS - KRW 20.0B treasury-share trust (12-08-2025 to 04-13-2026) bought 414,900 shares; all 444,368 treasury shares (incl. 29,468 from appraisal rights) were CANCELLED on 04-29-2026 (KRW 21,123M), shares outstanding now 50,970,126; FY2025 dividend KRW 650/share (KRW 33,400M, 25.3% separate payout, vs KRW 200 a year earlier); policy targets a >=25% payout ratio for three years and cash-dividend-centric returns, with charter amended 03-27-2026 to allow board-resolved share cancellation and quarterly dividends. (5) R&D - H1 2026 R&D spend KRW 37,645M = 5.58% of sales (KRW 65,864M in FY2025); 18 patents granted Jan-Jun 2026 including an i-line thick negative photoresist composition (02-03-2026), a new photoacid generator/photoresist composition and patterning method (04-01-2026), particle-defect removal and substrate-cleaning compositions (02-13 and 03-04-2026), OLED capping-layer/emitter compounds, a solar-cell patent (05-08-2026) and graphene-fibre and polyimide-film patents; battery pipeline (CNT conductive slurry, silicon anode, fuel-cell MEA) continues via Dongjin Sweden (accumulated impairment KRW 91,211M) and the 20.1%-held EVS Tech associate (KRW 1,519M impairment in H1). (6) INVESTMENTS - KRW 3.0B additional Picoentech convertible bond (05-29-2026, total KRW 5.0B, convertible into 366,667 shares); KRW 500M L&S K-Semi Renaissance fund. (7) FINANCING - KRW 30.0B Korea Eximbank export-growth loan (05-08-2026), KDB trade-finance limit raised to KRW 27.0B (05-29-2026). Board: CEO Lee Jun-hyuk (32.78% held via Dongjin Holdings); H1 TSR 60.85%; share price range Jan-Jun 2026 KRW 39,450-66,000.
